text:
This past week I was blessed to visit Falls Creek in Oklahoma. I’ve heard about it for years, but had never been there. It is truly an amazing place. Thousands upon thousands of teenagers come every summer to attend camp at Falls Creek, many surrendering their lives to Jesus for the very first time. It got me thinking about how important it is that churches be fully committed to doing whatever it takes to reach the next generation with the gospel…children, teenagers, college students, young adults…ALL of them. Why? Reflecting on my time at Falls Creek, let me offer 5 reasons (among many others):

1. Because Jesus told us to make disciples. The Great Commission includes those coming behind us. (Matthew 28:19–20)

2. Because the gospel is too precious to keep to ourselves. We have received the best news in the world that must be passed on to young people. How can we keep it to ourselves?! (Psalm 78:4)

3. Because every generation needs to know the faithfulness of God. They need more than our buildings and traditions. They need salvation…they need the Savior!

4. Because reaching the next generation is about reaching generations of boys and girls, men and women we may never meet. The young people we disciple today will disciple others, who will disciple others.  

5. Because reaching the next generation brings glory to God. When young people come to know, love, and follow Jesus, God’s name is honored. Our goal must be to make much of the God who saves, transforms, and remains faithful from generation to generation. Let all the earth praise His name! (Psalm 148)

Bottom line: We are called to faithfully pass the gospel from one generation to the next. Churches must think beyond “next year.” We must think beyond ourselves.

Bets considered for premium Saturday: 🔥 FREE PLAYS — SATURDAY, OCTOBER 3

⚾ FREE PLAY — CLEVELAND -159 over CHI WHITE SOX — 1:00 ET

Cleveland has enough independent support to make the free card.

One of our playoff systems applies to teams with a substantial rest advantage over an opponent that had to play through the previous round. Those teams are 25-13, winning 65.8% of the time when the price remains within the system's range. Cleveland had the bye while Chicago had to play the Wild Card round.

The Luck Gap provides additional, though modest, support. Chicago finished at +7.17 compared with Cleveland at +4.43. That's only about a 2.7-game difference over a full season, so it isn't remotely large enough to drive the wager, but it points in Cleveland's direction rather than against it.

The pitching matchup also supports Cleveland. Parker Messick finished the season with 193 strikeouts in 186 1/3 innings and recorded at least seven strikeouts in three of his four starts against Chicago. Cleveland also enters having won its last five home games.

The White Sox won the season series 7-6, so there was little separating these teams head-to-head. Cleveland's advantages were primarily on the pitching, defense and baserunning sides, while Chicago had the better offensive profile.

Play Cleveland to -165.

⚾ FREE PLAY — YANKEES +115 over TAMPA BAY — 6:30 ET

This is the most interesting regression play of the entire Saturday card, but there is enough conflicting evidence to keep it on the free card.

Tampa Bay finished with an extraordinary +14.61 Luck Rating, the highest in baseball. New York was only +0.95. That produces approximately a 13.7-game Luck Gap toward the Yankees. At a full-season sample size, that's enormous.

There is also value in getting New York as an underdog. Our official outlaw line opened around Yankees +114/Rays -134, and the market has remained in that general neighborhood rather than producing a major move against New York.

The concern is the pitching matchup. Drew Rasmussen's report card is outstanding: 16-5 with a 2.67 ERA and 0.91 WHIP. He has been especially effective against New York, posting a 1.81 ERA and 0.86 WHIP across 11 career appearances. In his most recent start at Yankee Stadium, he carried a no-hitter into the seventh and struck out 11.

Gerrit Cole counters with a 3.61 ERA for the season, but his Rays-specific report card is considerably better: a 2.50 ERA in three starts against Tampa Bay this year. He also brings a strong postseason résumé.

New York enters on a four-game winning streak and scored nine runs in each of its two Wild Card victories.

The enormous Luck Gap makes +115 attractive enough for a free play, but Rasmussen keeps it on the free card.

Play Yankees +110 or better.

⚾ FREE PLAY — YANKEES/RAYS UNDER 7 — 6:30 ET

Our top organic handicapper is on UNDER 7 and recommends it through -120.

The starting-pitcher report cards strongly support the position. Rasmussen finished with a 2.67 ERA and 0.91 WHIP, while holding opponents to a .543 OPS. His walk rate was just 4.8%, making free baserunners extremely difficult to come by.

Cole has a 2.50 ERA in three starts against Tampa Bay this season and a 2.93 ERA across 12 postseason starts as a Yankee.

Rasmussen's career performance against New York is particularly impressive: 5-2 with a 1.81 ERA and 0.86 WHIP in 11 appearances.

Tampa Bay's bullpen provides another layer of support behind Rasmussen. That becomes particularly important in a playoff opener where both managers can aggressively deploy rested relievers.

The price has become the issue. Some books have already dropped from 7 to 6.5, and we do not want to chase the move.

Play UNDER 7 to -120. At 6.5, pass.

⚾ FREE PLAY — MILWAUKEE -205 over SAN DIEGO — 8:30 ET

Free play because of the substantial moneyline price.

Jacob Misiorowski provides Milwaukee with the clearest starting-pitching advantage on the late card. He finished the season with a 2.12 xERA and 2.29 xFIP and closed with 13 1/3 consecutive scoreless innings over his final three outings.

His previous matchup with San Diego was dominant: seven innings with 10 strikeouts. He also recorded at least eight strikeouts in 19 of 30 starts.

San Diego's projected starting options do not offer a comparable report card. Milwaukee therefore owns a meaningful starting-pitching advantage without needing to manufacture a case from the relatively small Luck Gap.

The problem is price. Our official outlaw line was approximately Milwaukee -226, and the current market has actually improved materially for Brewers bettors, with -200 to -205 available in spots. That's favorable line movement from our perspective, but this is still an expensive playoff favorite.

Play Milwaukee to -210 as a free play only.

🏈 FREE PLAY — UCF/HOUSTON OVER 51.5 — 12:00 ET

A respected sharp played OVER 50.5 with a projection around 58.

Houston has been exceptional at creating quality possessions and converting drives into touchdowns. Quarterback Conner Weigman accounted for six touchdowns in the Cougars' latest game—four passing and two rushing.

UCF's 21-13 victory over TCU was deceptively low scoring. TCU outgained UCF 343-266, but four turnovers prevented those yards from becoming points. UCF also owns a strong rushing-efficiency profile that can attack Houston's vulnerability in preventing opponents from finishing drives.

The current number remains below multiple projections, but it lacks the elite systems corroboration necessary to move beyond the free card.

Play to: OVER 52.5.

🏈 FREE PLAY — MISSISSIPPI STATE +5.5 over ALABAMA — 12:00 ET

Mississippi State's offensive improvement has been substantial. Quarterback Kamario Taylor has accounted for 14 passing touchdowns and approximately 344 total yards per game, while the Bulldogs generated 499 yards against Missouri.

A respected sharp also supported Mississippi State at +6.

The major problem is Luck Factor. Mississippi State is +1.1, one of the highest early-season readings in the country. That is a meaningful regression warning.

With Alabama also receiving the expected public support, Mississippi State remains interesting, but the Luck Gap keeps it on the free card.

Play to: MISSISSIPPI STATE +5.

🏈 FREE PLAY — CALIFORNIA/UNLV UNDER 53 — 3:30 ET

Independent handicapping converges on a lower total. One model makes the game approximately 49, while another strong weekly report specifically identifies the UNDER.

Unlike Navy-Air Force, the market hasn't already removed four or five points of value.

That makes this the preferable secondary UNDER despite lacking the academy game's extraordinary specialized system.

The principal attraction is contrarian.

Kentucky is receiving meaningful public support despite being the underdog. That receives substantially more weight than an equivalent percentage on a favorite. Multiple betting populations identify Kentucky as the public dog, although the agreement is not universal.

Because the worldwide consensus isn't nearly as strong as Missouri or TCU and there isn't enough major system support, South Carolina fits better on the free card.

Naval tests (KRISO study) proved the 6:1 ratio handles 30m+ waves. Unlike the Wyoming, the Ark had no sails or masts causing twisting stress, and 3 decks of bulkheads prevented flexing. Continent-wide marine megasequences & polystrate fossils prove rapid global water deposition.

The claim that a 450ft wooden ship "couldn't float" ignores naval architecture. Testing by marine engineers (like the KRISO safety study) proved the 6:1 length-to-width ratio offers maximum passive stability, capable of surviving waves over 30m high.

Skeptics compare the Ark to the 450ft wooden schooner Wyoming, which leaked. But the Wyoming leaked due to twisting stresses from massive masts, sails, and a heavy steam engine. The Ark had no sails, masts, or engines, it was a passive hull with uniform stress distribution.

Structurally, 3 full decks with cross-bracing internal walls created a rigid cellular honeycomb box. This bulkhead design distributes load, prevents hull flexing (hogging/sagging), and provides incredible flotation dynamics.

As for flood evidence: continent-wide sedimentary "megasequences" show massive marine layers swept across entire landmasses at once. Add polystrate fossils (fossilized trees cutting vertically through multiple "millions of years" of rock layers), and rapid water deposition is obvious.

Trillions of marine fossils buried in massive bone beds on mountain peaks worldwide, combined with virtually every ancient culture retaining a global flood memory, point to one reality: Earth was flooded.

text:
🇺🇸 **TO THE SPORTS PATRIOT FAMILY... PLEASE DON'T LET THIS BE GOODBYE.**

I've spent much of today reading messages from our followers, and I want to take a moment to tell every one of you how much I appreciate you.

The messages have been pouring in.

Some of you are simply finished watching the WNBA for the season. Others have made it clear that you have absolutely NO intention of returning unless the league undergoes sweeping changes.

And frankly, after everything we've witnessed this year, I understand.

I've done my very best to respond to as many of you as possible. There have been so many messages that I simply haven't been able to get to everyone, but please know that your words haven't gone unnoticed.

**I AM INCREDIBLY GRATEFUL FOR EVERY SINGLE ONE OF YOU.**

Something extraordinary happened this season that I don't think enough people are talking about.

Caitlin Clark brought an entirely new audience to the WNBA.

But here's what the people running this league desperately need to understand...

**THESE PEOPLE MAY BE NEW TO THE WNBA, BUT THEY ARE DAMN SURE NOT NEW TO BASKETBALL.**

I've had the privilege of getting to know former college players, longtime coaches, referees, parents who spent decades raising athletes, basketball analysts, and fans who have followed this beautiful game their entire lives.

People who understand offensive systems, defensive rotations, player development, coaching philosophy, and what it takes to build a winning basketball culture.

And you know what?

**I HAVE LEARNED AN ENORMOUS AMOUNT FROM YOU.**

I've thoroughly enjoyed our conversations, our disagreements, the basketball debates, the research you've shared, and the friendships we've developed along the way.

Some of you have reached out privately. Others have contributed to discussions almost daily. Some have shared research, game footage, statistics, or perspectives I hadn't previously considered.

And some of you have simply been there, reading, encouraging, and supporting the work.

I appreciate ALL of it.

That's what makes today particularly difficult.

Because here we are, at the end of the Indiana Fever's season, and what are we left with?

The same questionable officiating.

The same inconsistent disciplinary decisions.

The same concerns about player safety.

The same coaching failures and inexplicable rotations.

The same organizational decisions that leave knowledgeable basketball people scratching their heads.

The same media narratives that too often seem disconnected from what fans are actually watching on the court.

And the same troubling questions about favoritism, accountability, and the institutional culture surrounding the WNBA.

**AFTER AN ENTIRE SEASON OF CONTROVERSY, WHAT HAS FUNDAMENTALLY CHANGED?**

That's the question I keep coming back to.

We entered this season hoping that the extraordinary attention Caitlin Clark brought to women's basketball would force the league to raise its professional standards.

Instead, we've watched far too many passionate basketball fans become so frustrated that they're ready to walk away.

And that absolutely infuriates me.

Because the WNBA has something special within its reach.

Extraordinary athletes. An audience hungry for basketball. Tremendous commercial opportunities. And a generation of young girls watching women compete on the professional stage.

**HOW IN THE HELL DO YOU MANAGE TO DRIVE AWAY THE VERY PEOPLE YOU SPENT 30 YEARS TRYING TO ATTRACT?**

I believe the league has allowed too many of its institutional relationships, personal loyalties, ideological battles, and internal politics to overshadow the basketball.

Somewhere along the way, parts of this organization began operating more like an exclusive social club than a professional sports league accountable to its players, customers, and fans.

And I am tired of watching people who genuinely love basketball being treated like the problem simply because they're willing to question it.

**WELL, WE AREN'T GOING ANYWHERE.**

And I sincerely hope you won't either.

Because while the Indiana Fever's season may be over, our work at Sports Patriot is only getting started.

🏀 **INTRODUCING OUR OFFSEASON ACCOUNTABILITY PROJECT**

Over the coming months, we're committing ourselves to digging deeper into the decisions shaping the future of the WNBA.

We're going to examine:

🔴 **LEAGUE LEADERSHIP:** The commissioner's office, executive accountability, governance, and the changes necessary to restore confidence in league leadership.

🔴 **OFFICIATING AND DISCIPLINE:** Rulebook enforcement, player safety, technical fouls, suspensions, inconsistent decisions, and the procedures used to hold officials accountable.

🔴 **THE INDIANA FEVER:** A comprehensive examination of coaching, offensive and defensive systems, roster construction, player development, front-office decisions, and the financial challenges facing the organization.

🔴 **SALARY CAPS AND CONTRACTS:** Veteran compensation, free agency, roster limitations, trade possibilities, upcoming negotiations, and how teams are positioning themselves financially.

🔴 **MEDIA ACCOUNTABILITY:** Television commentary, journalism standards, award voting, coverage of controversial incidents, and the influence of media narratives on public perception.

🔴 **THE FUTURE OF THE LEAGUE:** Expansion, the draft, competitive balance, fan retention, and the business decisions that will shape professional women's basketball for years to come.

And we're developing something I'm particularly excited about...

**A DOCUMENTED ACCOUNTABILITY LEDGER.**

A research-driven record of consequential league decisions, the rules involved, the explanations offered, and the questions that remain unanswered.

We're going to examine the evidence, challenge assumptions, and follow the facts wherever they lead.

And I want YOU to help us.

I'm inviting our readers to become part of this effort.

The coaches. The former players. The officials. The parents. The researchers. The basketball junkies who have spent their lives studying this game.

**WE NEED YOUR EXPERIENCE. YOUR KNOWLEDGE. YOUR INSIGHT. AND YOUR VOICE.**

We won't always agree. I wouldn't want us to.

Some of our best conversations have come from people challenging my analysis and forcing me to look at things differently.

That's how we get better.

And that's how this project can become something far more meaningful than one person sharing opinions on social media.

For those who would like to help support the research and participate more closely, we've launched **Sports Patriot Insider: The Accountability Project**, our new subscriber community.

We'll be sharing exclusive analysis, deeper research, investigative findings, and updates as this work progresses.

🇺🇸 **JOIN THE ACCOUNTABILITY PROJECT:**
https://t.co/jhpwLXYBzW

But I want to be very clear about something.

**YOU DO NOT HAVE TO SUBSCRIBE TO BE PART OF THE SPORTS PATRIOT FAMILY.**

Our public coverage will continue, and every single one of you is welcome to remain part of this journey.
But I want to be very clear about something.

Your support, whether through a subscription, a thoughtful comment, a research contribution, or simply sharing an article, means more to me than you probably realize.

I started Sports Patriot because I believe in honest sports, independent thinking, and the integrity of basketball.

What I didn't anticipate was how many incredible people I would meet along the way.

And I'm certainly not ready to say goodbye to any of you.

So to those who have told me they're done watching the WNBA, I understand. I respect your decision.

But please don't give up on the game itself.

The sport is too beautiful. The athletes have worked too hard. And the young girls who dream of playing professionally deserve a league worthy of those dreams.

**WE CAN WALK AWAY FROM A BROADCAST WITHOUT WALKING AWAY FROM THE FIGHT FOR BETTER BASKETBALL.**

There is strength in a community of knowledgeable people willing to ask difficult questions, demand consistent standards, and hold powerful institutions accountable.

And I believe we've only begun to discover what this community is capable of accomplishing.

From the bottom of my heart, thank you for an unforgettable season.

Thank you for the conversations, the encouragement, the disagreements, the laughter, and the friendships.

And thank you for reminding me why I love this game so much.

**PLEASE DON'T LET THIS BE GOODBYE.**

text:
America the Beautiful defines the nation as an ecosystem and a covenant rather than an ethnicity, which is exactly how biophilic and civic nationalism operate.

Biophilic nationalism saturates the text. Bates opens not with conquest or bloodlines but with "spacious skies," "amber waves of grain," and "purple mountain majesties." The country is literally the topography—the fruited plains, the wilderness, the "music-hearted sea." This is land-based identity: you belong because you revere the ecology, not because your ancestors did. The "halcyon skies" and "enameled plain" treat the continent as cathedral, suggesting patriotism is essentially environmental stewardship and sensory communion with the biome.

Civic nationalism anchors the moral architecture. The "pilgrim feet" reference is not ethnic but voluntarist—a "thoroughfare for freedom beat across the wilderness." The heroes are defined not by race but by sacrifice ("more than self their country love"). Crucially, the lyrics frame the nation as a perpetual project requiring active moral improvement: "God mend thine every flaw," "Confirm thy soul in self-control, / Thy liberty in law." The binding agents are law, "brotherhood," and shared aspiration ("crown thy good with brotherhood"), not genetic inheritance.

Unlike ethnic nationalism's closed bloodlines, Bates offers an open covenant. Anyone who treads the freedom thoroughfare, who builds the "alabaster cities," who accepts liberty disciplined by law and mercy, belongs. It is nationalism as gardening—cultivating the soil and the social contract simultaneously.

text:
CITY OF LIGHT

My First Completely Unofficial News Article From Las Vegas

By Jamie Stone, Project Stone

Las Vegas, Henderson, Clark County, what the fuck is up?

If somebody had told me this morning that by the end of the day I’d be sitting here writing what feels like my first Vegas news column, I probably would have laughed my ass off. I started Project Stone thinking maybe someday I’d have to run for Governor of this great state just to get my voice back. I thought maybe that was how you got the microphone. Maybe you had to run for office, win an election, stand behind some giant podium and finally say, “All right, Nevada, can we talk about what the fuck is actually happening around here?” But life apparently had another idea. Today I’m walking with my family near a high school, I meet a FOX5 reporter working a story, we start talking, and the next thing I know I’m giving this dude the Project Stone crash course right there on the street. 911. CAD. Public records. Government contracts. RFQs. Child welfare. Differential Response. Olive Crest. Casa Pacifica. Title IV-E. ASFA. Ground Zero. Social-media glitches. The Bucket Brigade. This poor motherfucker probably thought he was getting one quick conversation and instead got the Jamie Stone extended director’s cut. But here’s what mattered to me. He listened.

He asked me if I had been a firefighter when I went to the World Trade Center after September 11. Nope. I was just a man like him. Just a regular fucking guy who went there and did whatever I could do. That’s one of the most important things I’ve carried with me from Ground Zero. Nobody could do everything. Nobody was Superman. People searched. People dug. People carried. People brought equipment. People fed people. People did whatever job was standing in front of them. That’s the spirit behind the Project Stone Bucket Brigade. You don’t need Jamie Stone to solve the whole fucking world. You need thousands of ordinary people willing to grab the piece they understand, check it, document it, and pass the bucket to the next person.

Then I get home and see FOX5 talking about hiring journalists. Well, shit. Sign me up. I even offered the most attractive employment arrangement in American television history: I’ll start for zero fucking dollars. Before somebody screenshots this and announces that Jamie Stone is fraudulently impersonating the evening news, FOX5 has not hired me. I hired myself. That’s the joke. I’m the completely unofficial, self-appointed Project Stone correspondent until somebody with an actual FOX5 email address tells me otherwise. Hopefully we can renegotiate that zero-dollar salary eventually because apparently electricity, groceries, dog food and sidewalk chalk still cost money.

But it got me thinking about what news could actually be. What if people wanted to watch local news again because it was fucking interesting? What if we took complicated government paperwork and showed regular people why it matters to their lives? What if instead of screaming conclusions at everybody, we pulled out the original record and investigated it together? What if a reporter could say, “Jamie thinks A connects to B. Here’s the record. Let’s see whether Jamie is right.” If the bridge exists, show everybody the bridge. If it doesn’t, smash the fucking arrow. Put that on television too. I don’t want journalism where Jamie wins. I don’t want journalism where FOX wins. I don’t want Republican journalism or Democratic journalism. I want the fucking evidence to win.

I didn't dispute that. I began my response to you with: "That's true". 

My point was the Scots and the Irish are in alliance in the Remonstrance, with the Bruce offered the High Kingship.

Interestingly, the Remonstrance follows Robert Bruce's letter to the Irish Princes in which he spoke of Scotland and Ireland together as a Gaelic nation, "free since ancient times...sprung from one common root of origin" who are "urged and drawn more affectionately to come together in love by a common language and common custom".

In fact, when the Remonstrance was written, Edward Bruce had already been High King of Ireland for two years. 

Its not possible to separate Scotland from a central role in the Remonstrance, just as it's not possible to separate Ireland from being a central character in the declaration of Arbroath.
